
R programming for beginners. Manipulate data using the tidyverse: select, filter and mutate.
https://youtu.be/nRtp7wSEtJA?si=gYTjwzAubesA5gja

```{r}
install.packages("tidyverse")
library(tidyverse)

```
```{r}
#to see dataset available in R
data()
#lets use starwars
View(starwars)
```


Now we are going to try to get the BMI of humans in this dataset. to see the name of the variables

```{r}
names(starwars)

```

```{r}
starwars  %>% 
  select(gender, mass, height, species)
```

we want human only
```{r}
starwars  %>% 
  select(gender, mass, height, species) %>% 
  filter(species == "Human") %>% 
  na.omit()#to remove the missing value
```
lets change the height to metre
```{r}
starwars  %>% 
  select(gender, mass, height, species) %>% 
  filter(species == "Human") %>% 
  na.omit() %>% 
  mutate(height = height/100)
```

now lets create a new variable= BMI

```{r}
starwars  %>% 
  select(gender, mass, height, species) %>% 
  filter(species == "Human") %>% 
  na.omit() %>% 
  mutate(height = height/100) %>% 
  mutate(BMI = mass/height^2)
  
```

is there a difference between BMI of male and female? lets find out


```{r}
starwars  %>% 
  select(gender, mass, height, species) %>% 
  filter(species == "Human") %>% 
  na.omit() %>% 
  mutate(height = height/100) %>% 
  mutate(BMI = mass/height^2) %>% 
  group_by(gender) %>% 
  summarise(Average_BMI = mean(BMI))
```
